newsitem.title: INDIA: India shipwreck probe to be complete by end-July.
newsitem.headline: India shipwreck probe to be complete by end-July.

text.p: A probe into the shipwreck of the M.V. Arcadia Pride, a 13,672-tonne vessel that sank off the coast of Bombay last month, will be completed by the end of July, a senior Indian shipping official said on Thursday.
"We have started an inquiry into the incident and expect a report by the end of the month," Director-General of Shipping Michael Pinto told Reuters in an interview.
"We have taken the statements of all the owners, as well as the survivors, and I have given orders that the ship's position be videotaped," he added.
Officials said of the 33 on board the cargo vessel, six died, 18 are missing and the balance nine were rescued.

Pinto said the sunken vessel, carrying a cargo of sulphur when it suddenly sank in squally weather seven nautical miles outside Bombay on June 19, would not pose a danger to other ships entering the harbour.
"It sank at anchorage, and its position has been marked with a buoy as a warning to other vessels," he said.
Pinto said he would not speculate as to the cause of the disaster until the inquiry was complete.
"When the inquiry report comes in we will hang whoever is guilty," he said, vowing to take corrective action against the guilty parties. He did not elaborate.
